gemini_output_en.title: Comparing Stability Codes for Hypersonic Cone Heating in High Enthalpy Flows
gemini_output_en.paper_title: Stability Analysis for High-Enthalpy Cone Experiments in HELM and HIEST Facilities
gemini_output_en.authors: Viola Wartemann, Joseph Kuehl, Tony Liang, Sulav Kafle et al.
gemini_output_en.summary:
This paper presents a comparative analysis of several boundary-layer stability codes applied to hypersonic, high-enthalpy flows over blunted cones. The study focuses on two geometries: a 7-degree and a 10.9-degree half-angle blunted cone. The primary objective is to assess the influence of different numerical approaches on second-mode instability and to characterize the role of high-temperature gas effects. The computational results from seven distinct stability codes are compared against experimental data obtained from the High Enthalpy Shock Tunnel (HIEST) in Japan and the High-Enthalpy Laboratory Munich (HELM) in Germany.

The analysis quantifies the impact of high-temperature gas effects on the second mode and investigates the influence of uncertainties, such as minor variations in mean-flow conditions or wall temperature. A specific comparison is also performed between air and CO2 test gases, highlighting differences in stability characteristics under varying gas compositions. The paper provides insights into the agreement and discrepancies among the various computational methods and their ability to reproduce experimental observations under high-enthalpy conditions.

This work is significant for the aerothermodynamics community as it enhances confidence in computational tools used for predicting boundary-layer stability and transition on high-speed vehicles. A better understanding of second-mode instability and real gas effects in high-enthalpy flows is crucial for accurate aerodynamic heating predictions and the design of effective thermal protection systems for hypersonic missiles and reentry vehicles.

gemini_output_tr.title: Yuksek Entalpili Konilerde Sinir Tabaka Kararlilik Analizi: Deneysel ve Hesaplamali Karsilastirmalar
gemini_output_tr.paper_title: Stability Analysis for High-Enthalpy Cone Experiments in HELM and HIEST Facilities
gemini_output_tr.authors: Viola Wartemann, Joseph Kuehl, Tony Liang, Sulav Kafle et al.
gemini_output_tr.summary:
Bu makale, hipersonik ve yuksek entalpili akislarda, iki farkli kuntu koni (7 ve 10.9 derece yari acili) etrafindaki sinir tabaka kararliligini incelemektedir. Calisma, yedi farkli sinir tabaka kararlilik kodunu karsilastirarak, ikinci mod kararsizligi uzerindeki sayisal yaklasimlarin etkisini degerlendirmektedir. Temel odak noktasi, yuksek sicakliktaki gaz etkilerinin ikinci mod uzerindeki rolunu belirlemektir. Karsilastirma icin deneysel veriler, Japonya Havacilik ve Uzay Arastirma Ajansi'nin (JAXA) Yuksek Entalpili Sok Tuneli (HIEST) ve Bundeswehr Munih Universitesi'nin Yuksek Entalpili Laboratuvari Munih (HELM) tesislerinden saglanmistir.

Makale, cesitli hesaplamali kararlilik kodlari ile deneysel olcumler arasinda analizler yaparak, yuksek sicakliktaki gaz etkilerini ve ortalama akis veya duvar sicakligi degisimleri gibi belirsizliklerin etkisini nicelendirmektedir. Ayrica, hava ve azot test gazlari arasinda da bir karsilastirma yapilmistir. Bu analizler, yuksek hizli akislarda sinir tabaka davranisini anlamak ve tahmin etmek icin kullanilan hesaplamali araclari dogrulamaya yardimci olmaktadir.

Bu tur calismalar, yuksek hizli fuzeler ve yeniden giris araclari icin termal koruma sistemlerinin tasarimi ve aerodinamik isinma tahmini acisindan sinir tabaka kararliligi ve gecis mekanizmalarinin daha iyi anlasilmasina yardimci olur. Hesaplamali modellerin deneysel verilerle karsilastirilmasi, bu kompleks akis rejimlerinde guvenilir tahmin yeteneklerinin gelistirilmesi icin onemlidir.
